messages:
maya: FYI — after enabling INT8 KV + FP8 decode kernels for gpt-xl on the rtx-40 pool, p95 decode latency jumped in prod for warm sessions. Only shows up when a batch mixes very short (<=8 tokens) and medium (50-150 tokens) requests. Repro config: model=gpt-xl, kv_mode=int8, decode_kernel=fp8_mixed, batch_target=8

sam: Do you have a lightweight repro we can run on perf nodes? Also curious if this is PCIe copy related or an unexpected kernel fallback.

maya: Quick repro script (minimal):
```bash
# send a mixed batch: 6x short, 2x mid
curl -sS -X POST $RT_ENDPOINT/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"batch":[{"prompt":"hi"}, {"prompt":"..."}, {"prompt":"<50 tokens>"}, "repeat" ]}'
```
I ran it against rtx-40-staging-3. Attaching trimmed logs below.

sam: paste profiler summary? pprof / flamegraph lines are most useful.

maya: profiler snippet (trimmed):
```
Flame: decode_kernel_fp8_mixed 38%
KV_dequantize_path 22%
memcpy_async_pcie 11%
batch_router_wait 9%
other 20%
```
latencies: p50=95ms p90=170ms p95=380ms p99=800ms (when mixed)

diego: That KV dequantize path number stands out. Two possibilities: 1) calibration produced out-of-range scales so we hit dequant->requant shims, or 2) mixed-batching leads to misaligned tensor layouts that force slower code path (scalar fallback). Both cause extra memcpy/convert work.

jin: Also seen something similar on a smaller model last month. When seq-length variance in a batch > ~30, the kernel selector picks an FP8 kernel that assumes contiguous KV layout. If one request uses a different layout (padding pattern), we pay a runtime pack/unpack. That pack stage is O(tokens) but with bad cache locality it becomes a tail latency killer.

maya: Quick local microbench results:
- FP16 KV: mem=8.1GB, p95=120ms
- INT8 KV (calibrated with short-only traces): mem=4.2GB, p95=370ms
- INT8 KV (calibrated with mixed-length traces): mem=4.3GB, p95=150ms
So calibration distribution matters a lot.

sam: Interesting — calibration skew towards short contexts causes dequant error paths for mid-length KVs. That explains why mixed batches spike. Can you share the calibration artifact used for prod flip?

maya: prod used last_calib_2026-02-14.json (short-heavy). I did a quick re-calib with a mixed corpus and latency improved like above.

diego: That points to two mitigations: A) require calibration corpora to match observed seq-length distribution, B) change kernel selection to prefer fp16/fp32 for mixed-batch cases where packing cost > mem savings.

jin: Proposal (short-term): change batching heuristic to avoid mixing short+medium in the same device batch when kv_quant==int8. Pseudocode:
```python
if kv_quant == 'int8' and seq_std(batch) > 12:
    split_batches_by_length(batch)
```
This prevents triggers for the slow pack/unpack path and is cheap to implement.

sam: Agree. Also add a runtime gate: if pack_time_estimate(batch) > savings_estimate -> route to fp16 fast path. We have the estimator in batch_costs.py.

maya: I kicked off an A/B on staging: group A (split batches) vs group B (current). Early numbers: group A p95 ~140ms, group B ~360ms. Memory still ~2x savings for int8.

perf-bot: perf alert: job perf/repro-1798452100 finished. p95 reduction: -220ms for split-batching experiment.

diego: Long-term: we should make kernel selector aware of sequence variance and calibration confidence score. If calibration_confidence < 0.9 for a bucket, treat KV as "soft-fp16" for mixed batches. Also add a CI check that calibration corpora include N% samples with seq>64.

jin: I'll file an infra ticket and a runtime change. Owners: jin (batching heuristic PR), maya (recalibration job + artifacts), sam (kernel selector change).

maya: Created ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RW-4629 — notes + repro + artifacts link. I'll attach the mixed-calib json and perf traces.

sam: One more note — check NUMA/pci affinity for the node type. We saw similar memcpy_async_pcie spikes when the process fell back to a non-local GPU buffer. Confirmed on rtx-40-staging-2.

maya: Good call, I'll add NUMA checks to the repro harness and re-run. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

jin: I'll draft the batching-split PR and add a feature flag (opt-in) so we can flip without full rollback.

maya: Will follow up with final numbers tomorrow and close the loop on prod flip criteria.
